claims.episode_span: The 1,450-kilogram Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory reentered at 7:39 a.m. EST over northern Sumatra.

claims.claim: The X-70 Fractal cruises at Mach 0.75, reaches 45,000 feet, and offers more than 1,500 nautical miles range.
claims.episode_span: It cruises at Mach 0.75, reaches 45,000 feet, and offers more than 1,500 nautical miles range.
claims.source_title: NASA Announces X-70 Fractal, its Latest Experimental Aircraft
claims.supporting_quote: NASA provided some specifications for the X-70, saying it is designed to cruise at Mach .75, reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet, and provide an operational range exceeding about 1,726 miles (1,500 nautical miles).

claims.claim: Three firms received contracts worth up to $1.065 billion for Ka-band relay services, with Astranis up to $264.3 million, Global Enterprises Solutions up to $340.4 million, and Viasat up to $460.9 million.
claims.episode_span: Astranis was awarded up to $264.3 million, Global Enterprises Solutions up to $340.4 million, and Viasat up to $460.9 million.
claims.source_title: NASA To Develop Commercial Ka-band Space Comm Assets
claims.supporting_quote: The companies and their award limits are San Francisco-based Astranis Space Technologies Corp., $264.3 million; Reston, Virginia-based Global Enterprises Solutions, Inc., $340.4 million; and Carlsbad, California.-based Viasat, Inc., $460.9 million.

claims.claim: The Otter spacecraft lost its communications link during commissioning due to an issue in the fault protection system under a $15 million NASA SBIR Phase III agreement.
claims.episode_span: The Otter spacecraft lost its communications link during commissioning. The loss was traced to an issue in the fault protection system. The mission was testing propulsion, navigation, and inspection technologies for orbital debris under a $15 million NASA SBIR Phase III agreement.
claims.source_title: NASA-Backed Starfish Space Mission Loses Contact With Otter Spacecraft
claims.supporting_quote: Troubleshooting by NASA and Starfish determined the loss, which prevented re-establishing a two-way link, was due to an issue with the spacecraft's fault protection system.

claims.claim: Alex MacDonald, NASA’s former chief economist, was appointed CSA president succeeding Lisa Campbell and acting president Jean-Claude Piedboeuf.
claims.episode_span: Alex MacDonald, NASA’s former chief economist, was appointed CSA president. He succeeds Lisa Campbell and acting president Jean-Claude Piedboeuf.
claims.source_title: Alex MacDonald appointed Canadian Space Agency president
claims.supporting_quote: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly announced Wednesday that Alex MacDonald will be the next president of the Canadian Space Agency (CSA). MacDonald was NASA’s first chief economist and has spent the past year analyzing Canada’s space sector.

claims.claim: Cassini captured Enceladus in silhouette on November 1, 2009, revealing south-polar plumes that feed Saturn’s E ring, with 80-kilometer Pandora appearing faintly lit by Saturnlight.
claims.episode_span: Cassini captured the 500-kilometer moon backlit by the Sun, revealing south-polar plumes that feed Saturn’s E ring. Pandora, 80 kilometers across, appears faintly lit by Saturnlight beyond the rings.
claims.supporting_quote: One of our Solar System’s most tantalizing worlds, Enceladus is backlit by the Sun in this Cassini spacecraft image from November 1, 2009. The dramatic illumination reveals the plumes that continuously spew into space from the south pole of Saturn’s 500 kilometer diameter moon.
